newsitem.title: USA: U.S. machine tool demand rises sharply in December.
newsitem.headline: U.S. machine tool demand rises sharply in December.

text.p: U.S. demand for machine tools was estimated at $839 million in December, the American Machine Tool Distributors' Association and the Association for Manufacturing Technology said Sunday in a joint report.
The December figure was sharply up from November's $647 million estimate, which the trade groups reported a month ago.
"Other than the nearly $1 billion in orders posted during September, December was the largest month of the year," AMT President Albert Moore said in a statement.
"The $8.5 billion that our customers invested in new equipment in 1996 demonstrates their commitment to modernizing their domestic manufacturing capability," Moore added.
Total 1996 machine tool demand was estimated at $8.5 billion. The trade groups said year-to-year comparisons will be provided in the January report.

The latest figures were from the seventh U.S. Machine Tool Consumption report which replaced monthly data on U.S. machine tool orders, shipments and exports issued by the Association for Manufacturing Technology.
Machine tools are used to shape metal in making everything from bicycles to aircraft. Demand for these tools can provide a leading indicator of the pace of manufacturing.
The report said 3,543 machine tool units were ordered in December, up from 3,155 in November. Total 1996 machine tool demand stood at 37,569 units.

By region, the report said the Midwest accounted for about 45 percent of national demand, followed by 17.8 percent in the Northeast. The Central region accounted for 14.8 percent of U.S. demand, the South region 11.9 percent and the West 10.6 percent.
Export orders placed with U.S. machine tool makers totaled 284 units in December, up from 261 in November. Total 1996 export orders totaled 3,143 units, the report said.
